votes.reason: Confirmed from the code at 47b0382, no experiment needed. `retire_individual` (apps/app/supabase/migrations/0015_signup_eligibility.sql:247-257) loops over orgs where `created_by = p_user`, the user is `owner`, and `not exists (org_members x where x.org_id = o.id and x.user_id <> p_user)`. `check_retirement` (apps/infrx-api/tests/d/checks_signup.py:426-505) seeds t/n/o (uid group 6) only via `individual()` (0001 trigger: one personal org, one owner membership) and never inserts a second org or a second member for any of them, so the `not exists` predicate is vacuously true on every candidate row; deleting lines 251-252 leaves the same row set and every existing assertion (suspended, name='retired', one audit row) still passes. The mutant provably survives, matching the reviewer's `rv_retire_suspends_shared_orgs: survived` run. `signup_mutants.MIGRATION_MUTANTS` (lines 105-141) has no mutant touching the clause, and no test in tests/d exercises retirement of an org the individual created that has other members (the check at checks_signup.py:240 only proves a *bound personal* org cannot gain members, which does not cover a non-personal org like the 'side' org pattern at line 128). The "alone owns" scope is a stated invariant in the proposed R-A1 ruling (research/plan/evidence/a/A1-38aea7f.md:148) and the migration comment (0015:245), and the mutant's behaviour (suspending a shared org, so `set_suspension` refuses admission for its other members) is money/availability-adjacent. This is the same class the fix round itself treated as blocking for M-2 (claimed invariant with no killable test). The reviewer's minimal fix (second org created_by t with o as member; assert not suspended and name unchanged after retire(t); register the two-line deletion as a MIGRATION_MUTANT on signup_retirement) is sufficient and small.

Confirmed at 47b0382 by static analysis; no live run needed. (1) The invariant is stated: R-A1 in research/plan/evidence/a/A1-38aea7f.md:148 ("renames each personal org the user alone owns to `retired` and suspends it") and the migration comment at apps/app/supabase/migrations/0015_signup_eligibility.sql:245-246. (2) It is implemented only by the `not exists (... x.user_id <> p_user)` clause at 0015:251-252, and the loop scope is `o.created_by = p_user` (any org the user created, not just the personal one). (3) It is reachable: infrx.personal_org_binding_guard (0015:68-83) freezes membership only of a personal org that funds a wallet; a second org created by the user with another member, or a personal org shared before any grant (the rollout_hold case), is ordinary data. (4) apps/infrx-api/tests/d/checks_signup.py:check_retirement (426-505) builds t/n/o via individual() only, whose 0001 trigger creates one org with one owner row; the check never inserts org_members or a second organization, so for its dataset the loop's row set is identical with or without the clause, and the reviewer's mutant survives by construction. No existing mutant in signup_mutants.MIGRATION_MUTANTS (the six signup_retirement ones at lines 105-141) touches that clause. Same rubric as M-2 (invariant claimed, no killable test); consequence is a suspended shared org refusing admission for its other members. The proposed fix (shared org with created_by=t plus member o before retire(t); assert suspended is false and name unchanged; register the two-line deletion as a1_retirement_suspends_shared_orgs) is minimal and correct.

nonblocking.evidence: Probe P4a on BOTH images: conn A `select infrx.retire_individual(x,...)` left uncommitted; conn B `claim_signup_grant(x)` passes the retired check, then BLOCKS on the profile row (the wallet insert's FK KEY SHARE waits on A's FOR UPDATE); after A commits, B's ledger insert trips credit_ledger_signup_frozen and the claim RAISES `23514 CREDIT wallet ... is frozen: its owner is retired` (checks_signup.claim reports 'raised instead of answering'). Afterwards: claim -> retired, ledger 0, entitlements 0, retired 1. Money fails closed (nothing minted; the wallet row is rolled back with the claim); the backfill would count error:23514 and continue; A2's callback would see an exception and answer `retired` on retry. Reverse order (P4b) is clean: retire waits on the claim's transaction, then claim -> replayed with 1 ledger row.
